verses.text: Some time later, Jesus went up to Jerusalem for one of the Jewish festivals.
In Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate, there is a pool which in the Hebrew language is called Bethesda. It is surrounded by five covered porches.
A large number of sick people used to lie in these porches: people who were blind, people who could not walk well, and people who were paralysed. They were waiting for the water to move.
From time to time an angel would come down into the pool and stir up the water. The first person to step into the pool after the water was stirred was healed of whatever disease they had.
One man lying there had been ill for thirty-eight years.
Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had been in this condition for a long time. So he asked him, "Do you want to get well?"
The sick man answered, "Sir, I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am trying to get in, someone else always goes down ahead of me."
Jesus said to him, "Get up! Pick up your mat and walk."
At once the man was healed. He picked up his mat and began to walk. This happened on a Sabbath day.
So the Jewish leaders said to the man who had been healed, "It is the Sabbath. The law does not allow you to carry your mat."
But he answered, "The man who healed me told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
They asked him, "Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?"
But the man who had been healed did not know who it was. Jesus had slipped away into the crowd that was there.
Later Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, "Look, you are well now. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you."
The man went away and told the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who had healed him.
So the Jewish leaders began to persecute Jesus and looked for a way to kill him, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
But Jesus said to them, "My Father is always at work, even to this day, and so I am working too."
Because of this, the leaders tried even harder to kill him. Not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was even calling God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
Jesus answered them, "I tell you for certain, the Son can do nothing by himself. He can only do what he sees his Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does too.
The Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does. Yes, and he will show him even greater works than these, and you will be amazed.
Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son gives life to anyone he chooses.
The Father does not judge anyone. He has given the Son the task of judging,
so that everyone will honour the Son just as they honour the Father. Whoever does not honour the Son does not honour the Father who sent him.
I tell you for certain, whoever hears my message and believes the one who sent me has eternal life. They will not be condemned. They have already crossed over from death to life.
I tell you for certain, a time is coming, and has now come, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
The Father has life in himself, and he has also given the Son the power to have life in himself.
He has given him authority to judge, because he is the Son of Man.
Do not be amazed at this. A time is coming when all who are in their graves will hear his voice
and come out. Those who have done good will rise to live, and those who have done evil will rise to be judged and condemned.
I can do nothing on my own. I judge only as the Father tells me, and my judgement is fair, because I do not try to please myself. I want to please the one who sent me.
If I were the only one speaking for myself, what I say would not count as proof.
But there is someone else who speaks for me, and I know that what he says about me is true.
You sent messengers to John, and he spoke up for the truth.
I do not need anyone's human support, but I am telling you this so that you can be saved.
John was like a lamp that burned and gave light, and for a while you were glad to enjoy his light.
But I have proof that is greater than what John said. The work the Father has given me to finish, the very things I am doing, prove that the Father has sent me.
And the Father who sent me has himself spoken for me. You have never heard his voice or seen what he looks like,
and his message does not live in you, because you do not believe the one he sent.
You study the Scriptures carefully, because you think that by them you will have eternal life. Yet these same Scriptures point to me!
But you refuse to come to me to receive life.
I am not looking for praise from people.
But I know you. I know that you do not have God's love in your hearts.
I have come in my Father's name, and you do not accept me. But if someone else comes in his own name, you will accept him.
How can you believe? You enjoy receiving praise from one another, but you make no effort to receive the praise that comes from the only God.
But do not think that I will accuse you in front of the Father. The one who accuses you is Moses, the one you have put your hope in.
If you really believed Moses, you would believe me, because he wrote about me.
But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?"
